text: “I may say in conclusion that the Consulting Committee and General Managers are in no way opposed to the Reverend Father Robert's proposals, and I hope, therefore, that all present will vote against the confirmation of these resolutions so as to get them out of the way and leave us free to make other arrangements.”—With these words, Mr. R. As the Chan Kwing-ming army is retiring on its own account in preference to giving battle, General Cheung Kai-shek (the Cadet chieftain) has ordered Li Chai-sum (on the West River) to enter the East River war zone to establish himself at Tamshui.
[Note: The telegram hints that the Reds fear being enticed into enemy territory and there being enveloped. General Cheung will take command in person.]
Ex-Admiral Chan Chak (of Kongmoon and "Wing Fung" fame) has been appointed Director of Operations, under Chan Ming-shu, in the projected offensive against the Chan troops in the south of Kwangtung province.
A general strike has been declared against the Reds by the merchants at Fu Mun (Bocca Tigris) and Tai Ping (on the opposite bank of the Canton River). Over 10 strikers' pickets were killed in a squabble over an embargo on saltfish and this has caused the strike. The Red civil authorities on the spot have cabled Canton.

text: A large number of military and Government representatives, also many private friends, assembled at Queen's pier this morning to bid a temporary farewell to His Excellency Major General C. C. Luard, C.B., C.M.G., Officer Commanding the forces in China who left on the s.s. "Malwa."

label: text
text: Major General Luard is leaving for home to undergo treatment for his eyes and it is thought that an operation may be necessary. In his absence, Col. Russell Brown will act as Officer Commanding the forces in China.

label: text
text: The "Repulse" bethed punctually at noon to the salute guns and the cheers of the poulace occupying every vantage point.

label: text
text: The Prince of Wales waved his hat from the bridge. As it was raining hard, the Prince invited the Mayor and Corporation of Portsmouth on board the "Repulse" where they presented an address congratulating the Prince on the conclusion of his tour and expressing the belief that his visits to West Africa and South Africa had been of inestimable value in uniting and strengthening the Empire. The visit to South America would cement friendly Anglo-South American relations.

label: text
text: The Prince, replying, said his reception everywhere had been the kindest and most hospitable.

label: text
text: Subsequently in pouring rain the Prince was piped off the warship to loud cheers and the crashing of bands.

label: text
text: He entered the Royal train for London obviously touched by the warmth of his reception.

label: text
text: The King and Queen, Princess Mary, Prince Arthur, the Duke of Connaught and other Royal members of the family, Cabinet Ministers and diplomats welcomed the Prince who was accompanied by the Duke of York and Prince Henry who met their brother at Portsmouth.

label: text
text: On arrival at Victoria at three in the afternoon, the Prince, in the uniform of the Welsh Guards, was greeted by the King. He affectionately kissed the Queen.

label: text
text: At the conclusion of the formalities, the drive to the Palace was the occasion of wild scenes of enthusiasm and loud cheers.

label: text
text: There was a remarkable scene at Buckingham Palace after the return of the Prince of Wales.

label: text
text: An enormous crowd in front of the Palace chorused: "We want our Prince." Finally the King and Queen, the Prince of Wales, Princess Mary, Lord Lascelles, the Duke and Duchess of York, the Duke of Connaught, and Prince Arthur appeared on the balcon.

label: text
text: The King and Prince stood for some moments. Lare-headed, bowing and smiling.

All the points in dispute, including the Eastern question, have been settled.
The document embodying the Security Pact and the various arbitration treaties is at present being typed for initiating.
Locarno, October 16.
The Pact has been initialled.
Paris, October 16.
The Cabinet has unanimously approved the Locarno Pact and congratulated M. Briand, the Foreign Minister...

label: text
text: The concluding stage of the historic Conference was marked by the appearance of M. Briand and Herr Stresemann at the window of the Conference hall which aroused great enthusiasm among the spectators below. All the delegates were very warmly greeted as they proceeded in cars, especially Dr. Luther and Herr Stresemann, who were looking happy; but the greatest ovation of the day was reserved for Mr. Austen Chamberlain who entered his car holding the protocol aloft.

label: text
text: Mr. Chamberlain, speaking to British journalists, expressed his sole regret that the nations represented were unable to hear the moving delegations at the close of the Conference. The words of Herr Stresemann and M. Briand would remain an imperishable memory.

label: text
text: Locarno is en fete. The public buildings are illuminated. The famous monastery of Madonna del Sasso, on the hillside with the word "Pax" across the front presented a brilliant spectacle.

label: text
text: It is stated that the various foreign ministers will meet in London in December to sign the Pact.

label: text
text: The Prince of Wales aboard the "Repulse" arrived at Portsmouth at noon on his return from his tour through South Africa and South America. The "Repulse" was escorted by destroyers and flying boats. There was a slight haze and a drizzling rain. The ships in harbour were dressed with flags and the crews of the warships in harbour manned ship and heartily cheered.

text: The crossing of the road by a dog near the Western Market, Cananght Road, led to an accident which the Chinese driver of our No. 2279 bus reported to the police. In attempting to avoid the dog he swerved and a collision occurred between his and another car (No. 933) about to pass him at the time. Slight damage to the cars was due but no ong was injured.

text: The rainfall for the month of September at Botinical Gardens was 10ms.94 on 15 days, at the Matilda Hospital, Mount Kellatt, it was 5ins.25 on 14 days, and at the Police Station. Taipo, it was 5ins.50 on 7 days. The lowest barometer reading, at sea level, was 20ins.622 at 17h. on the 5th. The maximum squall velocity, as recorded by the Dines-Baxendell anemograph, was at the rate of 54 miles per hour at 0h. 58m. on the 1st.
